Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Maria Chen, CFO; Jordan Lee, CTO; and Taylor Brooks, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: advancing our product roadmap, accelerating MRR growth, enhancing churn management, optimizing our operating expense profile, and sharpening our full-year guidance.

Let me start with the product roadmap, which serves as the core engine behind our 28% year-over-year ARR expansion and our impressive 118% net retention rate this quarter. CloudForge stands as the premier AI-powered SaaS platform for enterprise workflow automation, powering more than 4,500 customers, including Fortune 500 giants like Pfizer, Deloitte, and Unilever. Our roadmap centers on three foundational pillars: amplifying AI functionalities, broadening our no-code/low-code ecosystem, and boosting global scalability to seize a slice of the $150 billion total addressable market for intelligent automation, according to Gartner's most recent projections.

Kicking off with our leading AI efforts, we rolled out CloudForge AI Copilot 2.0 in Q2, which has achieved 65% uptake among enterprise seats—rising from 42% for the prior version just two quarters back. This generative AI agent now autonomously manages 30% of standard workflow activities, such as contract reviews and supplier onboarding, slashing cycle times by 47% on average from initial customer evaluations. To put it in perspective, this echoes the momentum Salesforce gained with Einstein Copilot, yet we're distinguished by our industry-tailored models: take our Healthcare Workflow Model, which connects seamlessly with Epic and Cerner through FHIR APIs, delivering 92% accuracy in routing HIPAA-compliant data.

We're intensifying efforts with two key Q3 releases. First up is Predictive Workflow Analytics, hitting general availability on September 15th. Fueled by our custom transformer-based LLMs trained on over 10 billion anonymized workflow events, it predicts bottlenecks at 88% accuracy—for example, flagging a potential 15% delay risk in Q4 budget sign-offs ahead of time. Initial trials with our top 50 clients demonstrated a 22% improvement in on-schedule project completion. Next, Multimodal AI Agents enter beta in October, processing unstructured inputs from Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Google Workspace. This extends our addressable market by 25% into SMB territories, aiming for 15% share in the $20 billion collaboration automation space by FY26 end.

Shifting to no-code/low-code advancements, our Studio platform reached 1.2 million monthly active builders in Q2, a 35% sequential jump propelled by the Q1 debut of drag-and-drop GenAI builders. Studio customer NPS climbed to 74 from 62, linking directly to a 12% churn drop among users. On deck for Q4 is CloudForge Marketplace 2.0—a curated collection of 500+ ready-to-use apps and templates, modeled after Snowflake's marketplace but optimized for workflows. Collaborations with Zapier and UiPath will populate it with 200 integrations from day one, forecasting $50 million in partner-driven ARR by next year's close. This leapfrogs rivals like Workato, whose marketplace trails with fewer than 300 offerings.

Tailoring to regions, in APAC—where ARR surged 52% year-over-year to $120 million—we emphasized mobile-optimized tools for Japanese and Indian users; our Android/iOS Workflow Mobile app now features offline AI processing, lifting adoption to 78% in mobile-heavy fields like logistics. EMEA posted 41% growth thanks to GDPR-aligned Federated Learning in Copilot, preserving data sovereignty and securing 15 fresh DAX 40 accounts. In the Americas, vertical specialization shines: our Financial Services Module, automating real-time AML/KYC via Plaid and Trulioo APIs, accounted for 20% of Q2 net new ARR.

These moves foster sticky growth through land-and-expand dynamics—average ACV has ballooned 3.2 times from deployment, with AI driving 40% of upsells. Amid SaaS fatigue and economic pressures, our 'AI ROI Guarantee'—vowing 3x productivity or your money refunded—converted 85% of pilots to production. Our R&D commitment at 22% of revenue surpasses ServiceNow's 19%, backing a 150% surge in patents to 180 active in agentic AI.

Glimpsing FY25 and further, Q4 betas will introduce Autonomous Workflow Orchestration via agent swarms for complete processes and Zero-Trust Automation Security with runtime behavioral analysis to combat the 32% rise in SaaS threats per our index. These propel our 30-32% ARR growth outlook and NRR beyond 125%. We're not merely adding features; we're reshaping enterprise productivity for the AI era.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. On the financial front, including deeper dives into MRR trends, churn dynamics, operating expenses, and our updated guidance, I'll now turn the call over to Maria Chen.

Maria Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we delivered a robust quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin expanded to 82%, and non-GAAP operating income reached $42 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $320 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $540 million to $560 million.

To give more context on our core SaaS metrics, let me first discuss MRR trends, which highlight the reliability and vigor of our model at CloudForge. Monthly Recurring Revenue—or MRR—forms the backbone of our SaaS operations, capturing predictable subscription income from our cloud platform, encompassing workspace tools, AI-enhanced workflow automation, and our fast-growing Enterprise Analytics offerings.

We closed Q2 FY2025 with $45.2 million in MRR, delivering 28% year-over-year growth and a 5.1% sequential uptick. This marks our best quarter-over-quarter performance in five quarters, surpassing our 4-5% guide and accelerating from Q1's 4.2%. Annualized, this equates to $542.4 million in ARR, aligning with our full-year 25-27% growth trajectory.

Key shifts fueling this include net expansions contributing $4.8 million sequentially—94% of the total lift—with dollar-based NRR at 116%, up 200 basis points from Q1's 114%. This elite level matches top performers like Snowflake or ServiceNow in growth mode. Expansions stemmed from multi-year renewals and land-and-expand in Enterprise, averaging 25% seat growth post-launch. Notably, the ForgeAI Analytics module—live for 90 days—leverages gen AI for workflow predictions akin to Monday.com's project tools, adopted by 40% of top 100 customers for 18% average uplift.

New logos added $2.1 million MRR, up 15% sequentially, post our 25-rep sales ramp. We secured 14 deals above $100K ACV, highlighted by a Fortune 50 finance migration from Asana/Jira. Offset slightly by -1.8% revenue churn and 4.2% annualized logo churn in SMBs amid macro pressures; we've countered with stricter quals and AI-nudge freemium funnels boosting conversions 22%.

Geographically, North America dominates at 68% or $30.8 million MRR, up 32% YoY via AWS Bedrock ties and Marketplace acceleration. EMEA leaped 42% to $9.1 million (20%), on GDPR AI and DACH wins post-EU AI Act. APAC hit $5.3 million (12%), up 18% YoY but 3% sequential on FX; local JPY/AUD pricing and Tokyo DC address this, HubSpot-style.

These affirm our "AI Everywhere" push, embedding LLMs for 35% multi-product rise, plus "Unlimited AI Compute" at 60% enterprise attach. We anticipate 5-6% QoQ MRR in Q3, NRR >115%, with resilient enterprise demand and 90%+ incremental margins.

Next, turning to churn analysis—a vital measure of customer vitality and sustained value in our SaaS world. At CloudForge, we monitor logo churn and revenue churn meticulously. Our dollar-based net revenue retention—or DBNRR—stood at 118% in Q2, edging up from 116% last year, with expansions fueling 28% of ARR growth.

Breaking it out: Q2 gross logo churn was 4.2% (16.8% annualized), improved 15% YoY from 5%. Net revenue churn was -2.1%, as expansions outweighed contractions. Cohorts shine: 2022 acquisitions at 92% GRR, 2024 newbies at 88% vs. 85% historical benchmark. Multi-year deals now 65% of bookings, up from 52% two years ago.

Challenges persist. Economic pressures drove 35% of churn, with mid-market ($5M-$50M ARR) CIOs cutting costs—e.g., 15 Midwest manufacturers consolidated, losing $2.4M ARR (12% of churn). Product/competition caused 28%, especially SMBs on AI customization vs. n8n/Zapier ($1.2M fintech loss); enterprise contractions at 22% on seats. Onboarding issues hit 25%, with 45-day avg to 80% utilization (vs. 30-day goal), worse in EMEA (GDPR) and APAC (timezones). Regional: U.S. 3.8% (125% DBNRR), EMEA 5.1%, APAC 6.2% (China slowdown, 40% Japanese support). Other: 12% bundling fatigue.

Our response: $45M FY25 retention spend (2x ROI). Proactive CS: CSMs to 180 (1:150 ratio), ForgeGuard AI flags risks 90 days out—saved $8.7M ARR from 240 interventions; SMB self-serve cut onboarding 22%. Product: AI AutoPilot upped utilization 34%, usage pricing pilots trimmed contractions 40%; Q4 iPaaS marketplace. Pricing: FlexScale bundles boost enterprise wins 12%, freemium ramps convert 28%. Regional: EMEA OVHcloud (churn -22% QoQ), APAC Singapore hub/Alibaba (NRR +18%), U.S. verticals. Data tools + Growth Grants yield 45% upsells.

This outshines medians (Bessemer 110%; us +8 pts vs. Workato 112%), with enterprise to 130%. To $450M ARR FY26, NRR 122%.

On operating expenses, total OpEx hit $128 million, up 24% YoY but 2% sequential amid 28% revenue growth—Rule of 40 at 68 vs. Salesforce 52. Non-GAAP op margin +450 bps to 28%.

R&D: $52M (34% rev), +36% YoY, flat QoQ. 850 engineers (40% ramp) on: gen AI (ForgeAI GPT-4o/Claude-like, 70% task automation, 3x gains); multi-cloud K8s/zero-trust (hours vs. weeks deploy); edge/sustainability (EU CSRD). Splits: 45% US (Austin/Seattle), 30% EMEA (Tel Aviv/Dublin), 25% APAC (Bangalore). To 32% rev FY26.

S&M: $58M (38% rev), +26% YoY/+4% QoQ. CAC payback 14 mos (from 18), rep productivity $1.8M ARR (+22%), NRR 125%. Drivers: 120 reps (60% enterprise, $15M telco win); $12M ABM/6sense marketing (2.5x ROI), ForgeSummit 450 SQLs; regional (EMEA +45%, APAC +35%). Trending to 35-37%.

G&A: $18M (12% rev), +12% YoY/flat QoQ. Scales with 28% headcount to 2,200: SBC 9% (from 11%), Big Four compliance savings $2M, no M&A drag. 70% US. To 11-12% long-term; FCF margin 22% to 25% FY25.

This OpEx mix fuels outperformance toward 30%+ margins FY27.

Finally, on full-year FY2025 revenue guidance, we're raising from $500-520M (20-25% growth) to $540-560M (26-31% at $550M midpoint). Subscription ~95% at $515-535M; ARR end $550-570M (+32% YoY Q2), NRR 115-118% (vs. Bessemer 110%). Services $25M flat, gross 82-83%, Rule 40 55-60.

Drivers: Enterprise land-expand (ACV $450K+, 98% 12-mo retention); ForgeAI (15 $1M+ deals); multi-cloud/zero-trust (<5% churn); Q4 Marketplace $20M ARR; 5-7% pricing.

Regions: Americas $324-336M (60%, +30%); EMEA $135-140M (25%, +28%); APAC $81-84M (15%, +20%).

Confident in $50B+ DevOps TAM, 4.2x pipeline. Conservatism for cycles/FX/competition. Upside from AI/M&A.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan for a technology update.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Maria. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers—building on Kubernetes-native multi-cloud support, zero-trust fabrics, and edge computing to handle sprawling workloads efficiently. Our gen AI embeddings, like those in ForgeAI Copilot, are automating routine tasks at scale, while sustainability-focused carbon-aware scheduling supports EMEA compliance. These enhancements position us firmly as a leader in resilient, AI-driven workflow automation.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.

John Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

Taylor Brooks:
Thanks, John. ForgeAI has been transformative for our growth trajectory, contributing roughly 25% of our Q2 net new ARR through both new wins and expansions. It's accelerating customer value realization, with early adopters reporting 3x productivity gains that directly fuel upsells—average expansion ACV jumps 20% when attached. Attach rates are robust at 65% for new enterprise deals and 40% across our top 100 accounts for the Analytics module specifically. We're seeing land-and-expand play out beautifully, with 18% revenue uplift per adopting customer, and we expect this to drive another 5 points of NRR expansion in H2 as adoption broadens.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wang with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Wang:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Emily. APAC is a high-priority growth engine, representing 12% of MRR today but targeted for 20% by FY27. We're addressing localization with our new Tokyo data center for sovereignty, Mandarin support hub in Singapore, and tailored workflow templates for Alibaba Cloud—yielding 18% NRR lift early on. Mobile-first features and JPY/AUD pricing counter FX, while sovereign cloud focus drives ANZ/India wins. We've ramped sales 35% YoY, prioritizing high-mobility verticals like logistics, and expect 20%+ YoY revenue growth there, tempered only by macro.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays.

Mike Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Maria Chen:
Thanks, Mike. As I detailed earlier, we're tackling churn head-on with a multi-pronged strategy amid high rates—proactive ForgeGuard AI interventions saved $8.7M ARR, product innovations like AI AutoPilot cut it 15%, and regional tweaks like EMEA data sovereignty dropped it 22% QoQ. Gross logo churn improved to 4.2%, revenue churn -2.1%. NRR trends upward at 118% DBNRR (116% YoY), 116% dollar-based this quarter—elite vs. peers—and we see it expanding to 122% FY26, supported by 65% multi-year bookings and 125%+ in enterprise cohorts. Economic resilience in our sticky workflows gives us confidence.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
